customer: I'm trying to sell my late father's hybrid sedan so I can put the money toward something bigger for my family, and I keep getting the runaround. I have the power of attorney he signed before he passed, so why isn't that enough? My siblings are also asking whether they all need to sign, and frankly I just want this done.
agent: I'm sorry for your loss, and I understand how frustrating this has been. Per our article "Selling a car you inherited," a power of attorney signed by the person who died is no longer valid, so you'll need to bring the death certificate along with the court letters naming the executor or administrator of the estate (letters testamentary or letters of administration). If there are several heirs, the executor is the one who signs, so your siblings won't all need to sign. If there's still a loan on the car, please also see our article "Selling a car you are still paying off."
